extracted.intended_audience: U.S. EPA staff responsible for creating or reviewing Agency communications (public affairs officers, writers, designers, program/regional communicators)
extracted.subtask_description: Agency-level style and production guidance for preparing and reviewing EPA communications across most media, covering style, format, presentation, templates, logos, and the role of strategic planning and product review. Identifies which products the stylebook governs and which are exceptions requiring separate criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose: guide style, format, and presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: This stylebook is intended to help you, U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) staff, to prepare and review Agency communications. Our main focus is to guide the style, format and presentation of EPA's content and communications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the stylebook as the primary reference for how Agency communications should look and read; it is intended to reduce ad-hoc decisions about basic considerations so communicators can focus on creative and substantive aspects of projects. Note that some related formats (news releases, certain web materials) are covered by separate guides.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability to media and formats
rubrics_metrics.description: The EPA Stylebook provides guidance for most media, including print documents, audiovisual, broadcast, presentation and exhibit work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Style and formatting guidance in the book apply across these media; the stylebook also supplies templates, samples, reference documents, copyright requirements, information on publishing software, and required forms/processes. Where a media-specific exception exists (e.g., news releases, EPA Web site), consult the separate guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusions: formats directly covered
rubrics_metrics.description: The standards, practices and guidelines in the stylebook are directly applicable to the design and writing of: audiovisual, video and motion picture presentations; handbooks and manuals; brochures, leaflets, pamphlets and posters; promotional products; displays and exhibits; reports (see below for exceptions); fact sheets, fliers, handbills and announcements; and to the design of conference proceedings, non-English material (see Translation Protocol), criteria documents, technical research publications (see exceptions below), data-set and fact book publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When producing any of these product types, follow the stylebook's design and writing standards. Consult specific sections for templates, formatting rules, and any product-specific instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusions: formats not governed by this stylebook
rubrics_metrics.description: These guidelines do not apply to the design or writing of: articles for publication in media not controlled by EPA (including bylined/feature articles or letters to the editor by EPA employees and peer‑reviewed journal articles); contracts, purchase orders, solicitation of bids; correspondence (postal and e-mail); Congressional testimony; EPA Web site (materials created explicitly for the EPA Web site); guidance documents (official regulatory guidance); internal policy statements and directives; legal and regulatory materials (briefs, legal opinions, notices of rule making, Federal Register notices, notices of public hearings, regulations); news releases and accompanying materials; peer‑reviewed documents; and certain reports (Investigatory/Inspector General, Congressional, Science Advisory Boards, Administrative or fiscal reports).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although excluded formats may still use the stylebook where practicable, many of these require separate criteria and processes (notably news releases and web materials). Check the appropriate specialized guidance for excluded product types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plain language requirement and tone
rubrics_metrics.description: This stylebook is written in plain language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The stylebook models and promotes plain-language writing for clarity and accessibility. Use plain, direct expression in Agency communications unless a specific exception or legal/regulatory requirement dictates otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish mandatory rules from suggestions
rubrics_metrics.description: Much of the stylebook's contents relate to EPA and Government Printing Office (GPO) policy and must be followed as rules. Other contents of the stylebook are simply suggestions for you, fellow Agency communicators, to follow to create stronger communication materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When applying the guidance, identify which items are policy/GPO requirements (mandatory) and which are recommendations. Mandatory items must be followed; suggestions may be used at the communicator's discretion to improve effectiveness or consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for creation and use of logos
rubrics_metrics.description: This stylebook outlines basic standards and some detailed guidance to help you create high-quality communications, notably including standards for the creation and use of logos.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the stylebook's logo standards when producing materials that display Agency logos to ensure consistent and authorized visual identity; refer to the specific logo section for spacing, colors, and approved usages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Product Review system compliance and coordination
rubrics_metrics.description: Use this stylebook as an integral part of the EPA Communications Product Review system. The Product Review system is the communication management process that requires each program and regional office to ensure Agency communications serve the public interest and the immediate interests of intended audiences, as well as to ensure messages are coordinated fully across the Agency to convey EPA operations and policy with the highest degree of consistency and accuracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All products should pass through the Product Review process as required; reviewers should check that communications serve public and audience interests, and that messaging is coordinated and accurate across EPA. See full Product Review explanation for process details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic planning and development process
rubrics_metrics.description: Good communication is usually a product of research, audience targeting, media and format selection appropriate to the audience, careful strategic construct of the key message and the specific formulation of that message through words and graphics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply strategic planning at every phase — research, audience targeting, media/format selection, message construction, and production. Treat products as components of integrated campaigns built from these elements; use the pages about communicating from concept through production for stepwise guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrated campaign approach to communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Each phase of the development process applies to every product. EPA materials should be structured as multi-faceted, integrated campaigns that are constructed from those same elements of research, audience targeting, media and format selection, and message crafting from concept through production.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan communications not as isolated artifacts but as integrated efforts that align objectives, audiences, media, messages, and evaluation. This affects choices in format, distribution, graphics, and follow-up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation protocol and cross-cultural considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: For public information materials that are translated into languages other than English, or that are created, as original, in other than English, you should consult the EPA Translation Protocol.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While design guidelines generally should be followed for translated materials, be aware that cross-cultural communication may require changes to visual treatment and written/verbal approach. Consult the Translation Protocol for procedures and best practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of templates, samples, and required forms/processes
rubrics_metrics.description: We also provide several templates and samples, reference documents, copyright requirements and information on training courses, as well as information about publishing software, the general form of a publication, required forms and processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage provided templates and procedural resources to increase in-house efficiency, standardize output, comply with copyright and publishing processes, and reduce reliance on external services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expected organizational benefits of adherence
rubrics_metrics.description: Adhering to this stylebook's criteria for basic design and writing will help you: move more readily to decisions about substantive content, audience and media targeting and effective/creative presentation; reduce the need for more costly outside services by increasing in-house efficiency; standardize formats and sizes of products; economize on graphics and printing costs; and reduce waste and redundancy through common, centralized procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these stated benefits to justify following the stylebook within projects and to guide decisions on format, scope, procurement, and resource allocation.
